holding_summary: Homestead dispute over whether a widow who leased her homestead for a share of the crop, while keeping a room there, and a man who lived in a house on adjoining land, retained their homestead exemptions.
notes: Homestead-law case about a widow's share-crop lease of her homestead with a reserved room; not about compensated lodging/boarding of paying occupants.

holding_summary: Wife granted separation from bed and board based on husband's cruelty and threats.
notes: Domestic-relations separation case; no bearing on letting or lodging of dwellings.

holding_summary: Statutory mechanic's lien act did not impliedly repeal the Civil Code article granting a privilege to workmen who improve immovables.
notes: Mechanic's lien dispute over oil-well repair work; unrelated to residential letting or lodging.

holding_summary: Town's ordinance extending its corporate limits to include lumber-company mill quarters and an adjoining settlement was held reasonable, given shared community life and the need for uniform police and sanitary regulation.
notes: Municipal annexation case discussing sanitary/police-power regulation of mill 'quarters' and demand for 'rent houses,' but the holding turns on the reasonableness of the boundary extension, not on licensing or the legal character of lodging/boarding arrangements.

holding_summary: Mrs. Gray, who rented a house from Brown and used it as a boarding and lodging house, sued for damages after Brown provisionally seized her furniture for unpaid rent; the court held her claim foreclosed because she had already litigated and accepted a judgment on the same damages before a justice of the peace. The court also found her boarding and lodging business was not seriously affected by the seizure, since the furniture stayed in the house and boarders/lodgers continued to patronize it.

quotes.text: Plaintiff rented from James C. Brown the house which she used as a boarding and lodging house.
She contends that the seizure was unlawful, wanton, and malicious, and that it destroyed her business as keeper of a boarding and lodging house.
There were as many boarders and lodgers in the house when the seizure was released as there had been when it was levied.

In a landlord’s action before a justice of the peace for rent wherein defendant by re-conventional demand set up damages to her business as a keeper of a boarding and lodging house because of the provisional seizure of her furniture, and therein fixed the maximum amount of damages which she had suffered, and accepted the amount of judgment rendered in her favor, she could not thereafter bring suit for further damages for such seizure; her claim therefor having been foreclosed by the proceedings before the justice.

notes: Plaintiff was a tenant who rented the whole house from Brown by the month and sublet rooms to boarders and lodgers as her business; no specific duration of the boarders' individual stays is stated, so duration_of_occupancy is left unclear.

holding_summary: Dispute over a life estate/usufruct and reversionary interest reserved in a deed, and over rights between usufructuary and owner following a mortgage foreclosure sale.
notes: Usufruct/reversion and mortgage-foreclosure dispute; the 'right to lease' clause concerns a reserved life estate in land, not compensated room-letting.

holding_summary: Partition action among co-owners of town lots; court ordered partition in kind and held a co-owner who improved the property at his own expense need not account for rents collected.
notes: Partition action among co-owners over improvements and rents; no lodging or boarding at issue.

holding_summary: Trespass action for destruction of plaintiff's hedge and trees by neighbors acting as a road-improvement board; damages awarded against those who participated.
notes: Trespass action for destruction of a hedge and trees; unrelated to letting of dwellings.

holding_summary: Dispute over ownership of a plantation and a wife's liability for her husband's debts following a sale/retrocession scheme by creditors; court held the wife remained owner and was not liable for debts contracted by her husband in his own name.
notes: Boarding house is mentioned only as background — defendants induced plaintiff's husband to move and run a boarding house as part of an alleged scheme to gain control of her plantation — but the court adjudicates title and debt liability, not the legal character of the boarding-house arrangement.

holding_summary: Dispute over a party wall and whether a servitude of light and view existed between adjoining urban lots; court found no such servitude established.
notes: Party-wall/servitude dispute over light and view; no lodging or letting of dwelling rooms.

holding_summary: Lessees of a river landing used to moor coal boats were entitled to a reduction in rent after the lessor sold off part of the leased river frontage without their knowledge.
notes: Commercial lease of a river landing for mooring coal boats; not a dwelling or lodging arrangement.

holding_summary: Lessee of a public-market meat stall could not be barred by the city from having a competing telephone company install service to his stall.
notes: Market-stall lease and telephone-service dispute; not residential lodging.

holding_summary: Construed the term 'strangers' in the state inheritance-tax statute to include a surviving spouse, who is neither an ascendant, descendant, nor collateral relation.
notes: Statutory construction of inheritance-tax term 'strangers'; unrelated to lodging or letting.

holding_summary: Property temporarily moved into a third party's separately leased office in the same building did not become subject to the lessor's privilege for another tenant's rent.
notes: Dispute over seizure of property in a leased office within an office building; not a dwelling-lodging case.

holding_summary: Lessor's privilege on store furniture and fixtures survived the tenant's bankruptcy discharge because the furniture was never sold by the bankruptcy trustee.
notes: Lessor's privilege on store furniture and fixtures in bankruptcy; commercial store lease, not residential lodging.

holding_summary: A tenant who ran a rooming house was injured when plaster fell from the ceiling of her rented kitchen; the court held her landlord strictly liable for defects in the leased premises regardless of his knowledge of them, affirming $500 in damages while rejecting her unproven claim for loss of rooming-house business.

quotes.text: prior to the accident she maintained a large rooming house, that since the accident she has been unable to do the work necessary, and as a consequence has lost her business;
Her rent was $45 per month, and her income from twelve roomers was $35 per month a loss of $10 a month.

A lessor guarantees the lessee against all the defects of the leased premises even in case it should appear he knew nothing of the existence of such defects and he is bound to indemnify the lessee for any loss resulting from those defects.

notes: The court's holding concerns the landlord's strict liability for defects in the leased premises; it never adjudicates the legal character of Moman's subletting of rooms to her twelve roomers, so characterization and polarity are left null. Facts show she ran a rooming house paying $45/month rent against $35/month roomer income.

holding_summary: Possessory action for a wrongfully occupied vacant lot; plaintiff awarded damages measured by lost rental value caused by the trespasser's occupancy.
notes: Possessory action over a vacant lot with damages for lost rental value; no lodging or dwelling-letting issue.

holding_summary: A furniture company that entered a debtor's home during his absence and repossessed mortgaged furniture without legal process was liable for trespass damages.
notes: Trespass/self-help repossession of furniture from a residence; no letting or lodging arrangement at issue.
